input_signals.name: FragileAcquisitionSpend
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(aqc, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition spending by firms with weak operating cash flow represents fragile, potentially value-destructive expansion.
input_signals.reasoning: Acquisitions can create value when acquirers are operationally strong, but low cash-flow acquirers may overpay or use deals to mask organic weakness. This signal penalizes acquisition intensity specifically when paired with poor cash-flow quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( aqc, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LowMarginInventoryBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(invt, 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory growth is more likely to be unproductive when gross profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Rising inventory can indicate healthy demand preparation, but at low-gross-profit firms it may instead reflect overproduction, weak sell-through, or margin pressure. The signal targets investment in working capital that is unsupported by product-market quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( invt, 1 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashFlowFragileCapex
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(capx, at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capex is most likely to be value-destructive when undertaken by firms with persistently weak operating cash-flow quality.
input_signals.reasoning: This revision aligns the expected sign with the investment anomaly rather than treating capex as unconditionally good. The continuous cash-flow-quality interaction avoids collapsing weak cash-flow firms into a zero bucket and focuses the penalty on firms that both invest heavily and lack internal operating support.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( capx, at ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DeterioratingMarginPPEBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ppent, 1), at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Expansion of fixed productive capacity is more likely to be unproductive when gross profitability is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the near-mechanical asset-growth/accrual overlap with a capacity-investment channel tied to an independent product-market quality measure. High PPE accumulation paired with weakening gross profit suggests firms are adding capacity without evidence of productive demand or pricing power.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( ppent, 1 ), at ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternallyFundedCashFlowWeakExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ADD(RATIO(sstk, at), ADD(RATIO(DELTA(dltt, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at)))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Expansion financed through equity issuance and debt growth is especially value-destructive when operating cash-flow quality is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: External financing can fund productive investment, but weak cash-flow firms may issue capital to support unprofitable expansion or delay restructuring. The interaction focuses on financing-backed growth where internal operating discipline is absent.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( add( ratio( sstk, at ), add( ratio( delta( dltt, 1 ), at ), ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), at ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LowProfitIntangibleBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ib, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Recognized intangible-asset accumulation is more likely to be low-quality expansion when current profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Intangible increases often reflect acquisitions, capitalization decisions, or balance-sheet expansion whose payoff is difficult to verify. Pairing intangible build with weak earnings targets firms where such investment is less likely to be backed by demonstrated operating quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( intan, 1 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( ib, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashWeakCapexAcceleration
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(capx, at))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sudden acceleration in capex is especially risky when operating cash-flow quality is persistently weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This focuses on an investment ramp rather than the capex level, helping distinguish unexpected overexpansion from steady capital intensity. Weak internal cash generation makes rapid capex acceleration more likely to reflect aggressive or externally pressured investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( accel( ratio( capx, at ) ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LowMarginInventoryAcceleration
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A sudden acceleration in inventory intensity predicts weaker returns when gross profitability is poor.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts the investment leg from inventory growth level to an inventory ramp, targeting abrupt overproduction or demand miscalibration. Pairing the ramp with low gross profitability keeps the mechanism focused on low-quality working-capital expansion rather than normal inventory rebuilding.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( accel( ratio( invt, at ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityFundedWeakIntangibleBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-asset expansion is more likely to be low quality when financed by equity issuance at firms with weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Intangible growth can reflect valuable investment, but it is harder to verify and more vulnerable to overpayment or capitalization concerns. Combining intangible build with equity issuance and weak internal cash generation targets externally financed, low-discipline expansion rather than all intangible investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( delta( intan, 1 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LowMarginInventoryOverhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, at), 5)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory intensity near the high end of a firm’s own history is especially harmful when gross profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts the investment leg from inventory growth to an inventory-overhang state, capturing persistent stock accumulation rather than only one-period changes. Low gross profitability makes that overhang more likely to reflect weak demand, markdown risk, or inefficient production.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_rank( ratio( invt, at ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityBuildAfterMarginPeak
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ppent, 1), at)), RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 5), RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: PPE expansion is more likely to be unproductive when firms add capacity after gross profitability has already fallen from its recent peak.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids mechanically scaling sales by PPE and instead looks for late-cycle capacity additions after product-market profitability has rolled over. Such firms may be investing based on stale demand conditions, creating overcapacity risk and weaker future returns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( ppent, 1 ), at ) ), rank( sub( ts_max( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 5 ), ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LateCycleInventoryRamp
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, at))), RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 5), RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory acceleration is most harmful when gross profitability has already fallen from its recent peak.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the industry-neutralized restatement of LowMarginInventoryBuild with a late-cycle overhang mechanism. The signal targets firms rapidly adding inventory after product-market profitability has rolled over, which is more likely to reflect demand miscalibration or future markdown risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( accel( ratio( invt, at ) ) ), rank( sub( ts_max( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 5 ), ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: NonGoodwillIntangibleWeakCashFlow
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(intan, gdwl), 1), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Non-goodwill intangible-asset accumulation is more likely to be low-quality investment when operating cash-flow generation is persistently weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids treating goodwill growth as a near-proxy for acquisition spending by isolating intangible growth excluding goodwill. Weak operating cash flow makes such capitalized intangible expansion more suspect, because the investment is not being validated by internally generated cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( sub( intan, gdwl ), 1 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LowMarginInvestmentFundingGap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), oancf), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose capex and inventory investment exceed internally generated operating cash flow should underperform when gross profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal targets an operating funding gap rather than capex or inventory in isolation. Low gross profitability makes the gap more likely to reflect forced or unproductive expansion rather than temporarily high reinvestment by a strong firm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( add( capx, delta( invt, 1 ) ), oancf ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortTermFundedLowMarginInventory
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(GROWTH(invt, 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(lct, 1), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory growth is especially low quality when it is accompanied by rising current liabilities and weak gross profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN structure requires both inventory build and short-term liability growth, targeting inventory financed through near-term obligations rather than normal operating replenishment. Low margins make this funding pattern more concerning because there is less product-market profitability to absorb markdowns or working-capital stress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( growth( invt, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( delta( lct, 1 ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LossMakingInventoryBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(invt, 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory accumulation is more likely to be unproductive when undertaken by firms with persistently weak bottom-line profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the prior gross-margin-trend gate and tests a different failure mode: inventory build by firms that are already unable to convert operations into accounting profits. High values identify firms expanding working capital despite persistent losses, where inventory is more likely to become obsolete, discounted, or financed under pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( invt, 1 ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( ib, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtFundedCashWeakCapexRamp
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(capx, at))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capex acceleration is more likely to be value-destructive when it is accompanied by debt growth at firms with weak operating cash-flow generation.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the generic volatility interaction and focuses on financing discipline during an investment ramp. The MIN structure requires both a capex acceleration and debt-funded expansion, while weak operating cash flow identifies firms least able to support the new obligations internally.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( accel( ratio( capx, at ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( dltt, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtFundedInventoryOverhangWeakCash
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory overhang is especially problematic when it is accompanied by debt growth at firms with weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This combines an inventory-stock overhang state with a financing-stress channel, rather than relying only on one-period inventory growth. Weak operating cash flow makes debt-funded inventory accumulation more likely to represent liquidity pressure or unsold goods rather than productive working-capital investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( ts_rank( ratio( invt, at ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( add( delta( dltt, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LossFirmInvestmentFundingGap
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), oancf), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ni, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investment funding gaps are most value-destructive when firms also have persistently weak bottom-line profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the margin-drawdown conditioner that showed weak portfolio evidence and instead tests whether externally unsupported investment is especially problematic at loss-making firms. The MIN structure requires both an operating funding gap and weak profitability, rather than simply replacing a successful margin-level conditioner with a weaker late-cycle state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( add( capx, delta( invt, 1 ) ), oancf ), at ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( ni, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MaintenanceShortfallCapacityBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ppent, 1), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dp, oancf), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Fixed-asset expansion is more likely to be unproductive when operating cash flow does not cover the depreciation burden.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the external-financing and margin-drawdown recombination with a maintenance-coverage mechanism. Capacity build is most suspect when existing assets already consume more depreciation than the firm generates in operating cash flow, suggesting expansion on top of an under-earning asset base.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( ppent, 1 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dp, oancf ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AcquisitionOutspendsCashFlow
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(aqc, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(aqc, oancf), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition spending is especially risky when acquisition outlays exceed internally generated operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This distinguishes cash-flow-supported acquisition activity from deals that require funding beyond current operating capacity. High values require both meaningful acquisition investment and a large acquisition-versus-OCF gap, directly testing financing discipline in acquired growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( aqc, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( aqc, oancf ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ReceivableLikeBuildLowMargin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, invt), che), 1), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Non-cash, non-inventory current-asset growth is more suspect when gross profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the failed cash-hoarding channel by excluding both cash and inventory from the current-asset build. The remaining current-asset expansion is closer to receivables and prepaids, which can indicate aggressive working-capital expansion or weak collections when margins are already poor.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, invt ), che ), 1 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualIntangibleOverhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(intan, at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High intangible-asset intensity is more suspect when earnings are not supported by operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the sparse non-goodwill funding-gap construction and the retained-earnings overlay that risked becoming a weak-cash-flow proxy. The mechanism is balance-sheet capitalization risk: firms carrying unusually high intangible assets while relying on accrual-heavy earnings may be overstating the productivity of past investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_rank( ratio( intan, at ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortDebtInventoryBuildLowMargin
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(GROWTH(invt, 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory growth is more likely to be low quality when accompanied by short-term debt growth at low-margin firms.
input_signals.reasoning: This distinguishes inventory financed by explicit short-term borrowing from inventory financed through normal payables or internal cash. Weak gross profitability increases the risk that the borrowed working-capital build becomes a liquidity problem or requires markdowns.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( growth( invt, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: InventoryWeightedFundingGap
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(invt, 1), ADD(capx, ABS(DELTA(invt, 1))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investment funding gaps are most problematic when the unsupported investment is concentrated in inventory build rather than fixed-capital spending.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a time-window smoothing of the prior funding-gap signal; it tests the composition of the gap. A funding shortfall tied to inventory accumulation is more likely to reflect unsold goods and working-capital stress than a transitory capex timing mismatch.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( add( capx, delta( invt, 1 ) ), oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( delta( invt, 1 ), add( capx, abs( delta( invt, 1 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapexRampIntoInventoryOverhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(capx, at))), RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, at), 5))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capex acceleration is more likely to be value-destructive when firms already have inventory overhang and weak gross profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the depreciation-minus-cash-flow conditioner that collapsed toward weak OCF and instead tests a demand-absorption mechanism. Firms ramping capital spending while inventories are already elevated and margins are weak are more likely expanding capacity into overstocked, low-return product markets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( accel( ratio( capx, at ) ) ), rank( ts_rank( ratio( invt, at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityBuildAfterDepreciationLoss
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ppent, 1), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), dp), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Fixed-asset expansion is more likely to be unproductive when gross profit is weak after covering depreciation burden.
input_signals.reasoning: Firms adding PPE while gross profit barely covers depreciation may be expanding an under-earning asset base. This targets a capital-productivity and replacement-treadmill mechanism without relying on the weak-operating-cash-flow conditioner that can dominate maintenance-shortfall signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( ppent, 1 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), dp ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ReceivableTurnoverOverhangLowMargin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, invt), che), sale), 5)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A high own-history stock of receivable-like current assets relative to sales is more suspect when gross profitability is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the short-debt MIN gate that risked being dominated by sparse debt changes and shifts from a one-period receivable-like build to a turnover-overhang state. Low margins make the receivable-like asset overhang more concerning because weak product economics leave less room for collection problems, concessions, or aggressive revenue recognition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_rank( ratio( sub( sub( act, invt ), che ), sale ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ) ) ) )
